ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Put maize seeds under conditions of 25℃, darkness, and suitable water for germination. At fixed times each day, take the same number of germinating seeds; dry and weigh half of them directly, and cut out the endosperm from the other half, dry and weigh it, and calculate the average dry weight per seed. The results are shown in the figure. If only considering that the nutrients needed for seed germination come from the endosperm, answer the question according to the figure: during germination, between which time period is the respiration rate of the seeds the greatest, and during this time period how many mg is the average dry weight consumed by respiration per seed?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The respiration rate of the seeds is greatest between 72-96 hours, and the average dry weight is 26.5mg

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the horizontal axis in the figure is germination time, marked 0, 24, 48, 72, 96, and 120 h; the vertical axis is average dry weight per seed (mg). There are two curves in the figure; the upper curve is labeled "germinating seeds", and its data are approximately 221.3, 205.9, 205.3, 204.2, 177.7, and 172.7 mg; the lower curve is labeled "endosperm". Then reason: the stem states that germination occurs under dark conditions, and that only considering that the nutrients needed for seed germination come from the endosperm, so the decrease in total dry weight of germinating seeds can be regarded as organic matter consumed by respiration. Calculate segment by segment the dry-weight decrease of the upper "germinating seeds" curve every 24 hours: 0–24 h is 221.3−205.9=15.4 mg; 24–48 h is 205.9−205.3=0.6 mg; 48–72 h is 205.3−204.2=1.1 mg; 72–96 h is 204.2−177.7=26.5 mg; 96–120 h is 177.7−172.7=5.0 mg. Comparison shows that the decrease from 72–96 h is the largest, so the respiration rate is greatest during this time period; the average dry weight consumed by respiration per seed during this time period is 26.5 mg.
